property_summary: After initialize returns successfully, the nft getter equals the _nft argument passed (reference always sets nft before emitting, but the mutant emits before assigning nft so observable nft may remain zero during/at emit); the reference guarantees c.nft() == _nft after initialize for every input while the mutant can leave nft unset during the emitted Initialize event and thus c.nft() != _nft for some inputs.

For every call to initialize(...) that succeeds, the contract's public getter nft() equals the _nft argument passed (the reference always stores nft before emitting/returning); the mutant that emits Initialize before assigning nft can result in nft() != _nft for some inputs.

For any inputs that successfully initialize the pool, after initialize(...) returns the public getter nft() equals the _nft argument; the mutant that emits the Initialize event before assigning nft can leave nft() different from _nft for some inputs (observable via the public getter).

For any inputs that successfully return from initialize(...), the emitted Initialize event's second indexed topic (the nft argument) must equal the contract's nft() getter after the call; the mutant emits the event before storing nft, so for some inputs the event's nft value differs from the stored nft.

For any inputs that successfully return from initialize(...), calling the contract's public nft() getter must equal the _nft argument (the reference sets nft before emitting/returning); the mutant that emits the Initialize event before assigning nft can leave nft() != _nft for some inputs, so there exists an input where nft() != _nft after initialize returns.

For any admissible _feeRate passed to initialize, the contract's stored feeRate equals the provided _feeRate (i.e. initialize stores feeRate exactly); the mutant caps values > 5000 so for some fuzzed _feeRate the stored feeRate will differ and the property is violated.

For every admissible _feeRate (0..5000) passed to initialize, the deployed contract stores feeRate equal to the provided value; the mutant instead caps values >5000 which causes stored feeRate to differ when a caller supplies a value >5000 (the bug is exposed by fuzzing _feeRate above 5000).

For any _feeRate input the initialize call emits an Initialize event whose logged feeRate argument equals the caller-provided _feeRate; the mutant stores a capped feeRate (5000) but still emits the original _feeRate in the event, causing a mismatch between the emitted feeRate and the stored feeRate for some inputs.

For any call to initialize where _feeRate is within the constructor-allowed bound (<= 5000), the stored feeRate equals the provided _feeRate; the mutant (which caps stored feeRate to 5000 regardless) preserves this for <=5000 but will cause the stored feeRate to differ from the provided value when _feeRate > 5000 — to expose the mutant we assert that when initialize succeeds (no revert) the stored feeRate equals the provided _feeRate iff the provided _feeRate <= 5000, which the reference always satisfies and the mutant violates for some inputs.

For any uint16 feeRate input to initialize, if the call succeeds then the stored c.feeRate() equals the provided _feeRate (reference always stores exactly the provided value); the mutant that caps stored feeRate to 5000 will cause a mismatch for some inputs (when provided _feeRate > 5000) so the property fails on the mutant.

For any inputs to initialize, the reference contract sets initialized == true after a successful initialize call; the mutant that removed the assignment may leave initialized == false after initialize, so the property is that initialize always sets initialized to true (the mutant violates this for some inputs).

After any successful call to initialize(...) the contract's public boolean initialized must be true (reference always sets initialized before/at observable effects), but the mutant that defers setting initialized until after emitting Initialize can leave initialized == false observable to external callers that react to the event, so the mutant violates that rule for some inputs.
